AI for Supply Chain

Explore how data and AI connect demand, suppliers, production, distribution and customer service.

Browse slides

From linear processes to a connected ecosystem

This presentation maps AI opportunities across the supply chain, from demand sensing and supplier selection to manufacturing, transportation and customer support. It also introduces implementation challenges, sustainability, risk management and the relationship between supply chains and value chains.

The original slides are preserved below, with thumbnail navigation and expandable text for each slide.

Key themes

  • Connect demand signals, inventory, production schedules and orders.
  • Explore predictive maintenance, quality control and supplier risk assessment.
  • Coordinate transportation, warehousing, fulfillment and returns.
  • Address data quality, adoption, privacy and security.
  • Understand value-chain activities alongside supply-chain operations.

Frequently asked questions

What supply chain areas does this deck cover?

The presentation covers demand sensing and forecasting, procurement, supplier selection, production, inventory, logistics, customer service and returns.

Which industries are included?

The opening slide identifies retail, food and beverage, manufacturing, healthcare and consumer electronics.

What AI applications are highlighted?

Examples in the deck include predictive analytics, supplier risk assessment, digital twins, predictive maintenance, quality control, inventory optimization and route optimization.

What implementation challenges are discussed?

The slides identify data challenges, implementation and adoption, and data privacy and security as areas requiring attention.

How does the deck compare supply chains and value chains?

The supply chain diagram follows sourcing, logistics, production and delivery to customers. The value chain discussion also highlights planning, innovation, product development and customer satisfaction, followed by categories and primary activities.
